title: Covalent anchoring of tethered ligands to chemogenetic handles for targeted in vivo neuropharmacology
author: Ciscato, Stenbolt, et al.
materials:
•Add 9 g of Sodium Chloride (NaCl; Sigma-Aldrich S7653) and 950 mL of milli-Q water to a 1 L bottle.•Stir at medium speed until fully dissolved and adjust the volume up to 1 L with milli-Q water.•Filter the solution using a 50 mL syringe (Terumo Luer Lock Syringe, 50 mL) and an appropriate syringe filter, such as Nalgene 25 mm syringe filter (Sterile Nylon membrane, 0.2 μm pore size).
Note: Store the bottle at 4°C (up to 1 year – date the bottle).

•To prepare 100 mL of an 8% (w/v) solution, weigh out 8 grams of chloral hydrate powder (Sigma-Aldrich 15307).•Add the powder to 80 mL of milli-Q water in a beaker or flask.•Stir the solution using a magnetic stir bar until the powder is completely dissolved.•Transfer the solution to a graduated cylinder or volumetric flask and add milli-Q water to bring the final volume up to 100 mL.•Filter the solution through a 0.22 μm sterile syringe filter into a sterile container. Store at 4°C and protect from light.
Note: Chloral hydrate is hazardous and should be handled with appropriate PPE. Safer alternatives, such as isoflurane, may be used if preferred or required by institutional guidelines.

steps.title: Prepare MPEG4Ch 50 mM stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 9.87 mg MPEG4Ch chloride (MW = 394.9 g·mol⁻¹) with a clean dry spatula, transfer to a sterile micro‑centrifuge tube, add 500 µL freshly opened anhydrous DMSO (must be unopened to avoid moisture), mix gently by pipetting or vortexing until fully dissolved, aliquot 10 µL portions into clearly labeled 0.2 mL Eppendorf tubes, store aliquots at –20 °C, minimize air exposure and avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare filtered 0.9 % saline
steps.instruction: Add 9 g NaCl (Sigma‑Aldrich S7653) to 950 mL milli‑Q water in a 1 L bottle, stir at medium speed until fully dissolved, adjust the volume to 1 L with milli‑Q water, filter the solution through a 0.2 µm sterile nylon syringe filter (e.g., Nalgene 25 mm), store the bottle at 4 °C (up to 1 year, date the bottle).

steps.title: Prepare nicotine tartrate 57 mg/L
steps.instruction: Pour 100 mL sterile filtered 0.9 % saline into a clean beaker, add 5.7 mg nicotine hydrogen tartrate (Glentham LifeSciences GL9693, MW = 462.41 g·mol⁻¹), stir until completely dissolved, adjust pH to 7.2 ± 0.2 with NaOH as needed, note that 0.1 mL injection per 10 g body weight delivers 0.2 mg·kg⁻¹ nicotine free base (10 mL·kg⁻¹), prepare fresh weekly or make a more concentrated stock, aliquot and store at –20 °C, thaw and dilute to working concentration when needed.

steps.title: Prepare aCSF 10× stock
steps.instruction: Place a clean 1 L beaker with a magnetic stir bar on a stirring plate, add 500 mL milli‑Q water, then add NaCl 125.0 g, KCl 25.1 g, NaH₂PO₄ 12.5 g, and NaHCO₃ 21.85 g while stirring until fully dissolved. Transfer to a clean 1 L volumetric flask, bring to 1 L with milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.2 µm membrane bottle‑top filter (Nalgene), label, store at 4 °C and use within 30 days.

steps.title: Prepare aCSF 1× working solution
steps.instruction: In a clean 1 L beaker with magnetic stir bar, add 500 mL milli‑Q water, then add CaCl₂·2H₂O (2 M) 21 mL, MgCl₂·6H₂O (2 M) 10.5 mL, glucose 10 g, sucrose 101.98 g, and 100 mL aCSF 10× stock solution; rinse the volumetric flask with a small amount of milli‑Q water and add the rinse to the beaker. Transfer the mixture to a clean 1 L volumetric flask, bring to 1 L with milli‑Q water, invert several times to mix, transfer to a clean 1 L bottle, store at 4 °C and use within 3 days.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose‑based cutting solution
steps.instruction: In a clean 1 L beaker with magnetic stir bar, add 500 mL milli‑Q water, then add MgCl₂·6H₂O (2 M) 5.92 mL, glucose 0.49 g, sucrose 100 mL aCSF 10× stock, rinse the volumetric flask and add the rinse, transfer to a clean 1 L volumetric flask, bring to 1 L with milli‑Q water, invert several times, pour into a clean 1 L storage bottle, weigh 200 mg kynurenic acid and add to the solution, sonicate for 15 min to dissolve completely, store at 4 °C and use within 3 days.

steps.title: Prepare K‑gluconate internal solution
steps.instruction: Place a clean 50 mL glass beaker with magnetic stir bar on a stir plate, add 35 mL milli‑Q water, then sequentially add K‑gluconate 135 g, HEPES free acid 19.15 mg, KCl 75 mg, MgCl₂ 22 mg, EGTA 0.33 mg, Mg‑ATP 18 mg while stirring until fully dissolved. Adjust pH to 7.2 with small volumes of 0.1–1 M HCl, transfer to a 50 mL volumetric flask, bring to 50 mL with milli‑Q water, seal with Parafilm, gently invert to mix, filter‑sterilize through a 0.2 µm syringe filter into a sterile container, aliquot 0.5 mL into labeled 0.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, store at –20 °C, use within 6 months, thaw on day of experiment and do not refreeze; discard any remaining solution after the recording session.

steps.title: Prepare 8 % chloral hydrate anesthesia
steps.instruction: Weigh 8 g chloral hydrate powder (Sigma‑Aldrich 15307), add to 80 mL milli‑Q water in a beaker, stir with a magnetic stir bar until completely dissolved, transfer to a graduated cylinder or volumetric flask and bring to 100 mL with milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.22 µm sterile syringe filter into a sterile container, store at 4 °C protected from light; handle with appropriate PPE as chloral hydrate is hazardous (alternatives such as isoflurane may be used per institutional guidelines).

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse and perfuse
steps.instruction: Inject intraperitoneally a mixture of 0.11 mL ketamine (100 mg·mL⁻¹) + 0.06 mL xylazine (20 mg·mL⁻¹) in 0.63 mL sterile NaCl, confirm loss of pedal reflex, open thoracic cavity, inject 0.1 mL heparin (1000 U·mL⁻¹) into the heart apex, clamp the descending aorta, perfuse with ice‑cold oxygenated sucrose‑based cutting solution using a peristaltic pump for 1 min 20 sec.

steps.title: Dissect brain and cut slices
steps.instruction: Decapitate the mouse, extract the brain, immediately submerge in 0 °C oxygenated cutting solution, place ventral side down on filter paper and make two coronal cuts (behind olfactory bulbs and through cerebellum), affix the rostral section onto the Compresstome specimen holder with glue and agarose, fill the slicing chamber with 150 mL ice‑cold oxygenated cutting solution, slice at 250 µm thickness, transfer IPN‑containing slices to a 35 °C oxygenated sucrose‑based recovery solution for 8 min (repeat for 2–3 slices per brain), then move slices to oxygenated 1× aCSF kept at 20–25 °C and incubate for at least 60 min. Clean all dissection instruments with distilled water and, when appropriate, 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Incubate slices with MPEG4Ch
steps.instruction: Freshly prepare 700 µL 1× aCSF containing 50 µM MPEG4Ch by diluting 0.7 µL of the 50 mM MPEG4Ch stock (DMSO) into 700 µL 1× aCSF; prepare this solution on the day of the experiment and avoid freeze‑thaw cycles. After the recovery period, place each IPN slice in a 12‑well plate containing oxygenated 1× aCSF, remove the existing aCSF with a transfer pipette and immediately add the 700 µL MPEG4Ch‑aCSF, incubate for 10 min under constant oxygenation.

steps.title: Rinse slices three times
steps.instruction: Remove the MPEG4Ch‑containing solution and replace with 700 µL fresh oxygenated 1× aCSF, let the slice rest for 3 min; repeat this rinsing step two additional times for a total of three rinses, then transfer the slice to the patch‑clamp recording chamber, handling the slice with extreme care to avoid damage.

steps.title: Pull and fill patch pipettes
steps.instruction: Pull patch pipettes (3–6 MΩ) from borosilicate glass capillaries (G150TF‑3, Warner Instruments) using a P‑87 puller (Sutter Instruments). Thaw an aliquot of K‑gluconate internal solution, draw it into a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 4 µm Nalgene syringe filter and a microloader, fill each pipette until the solution reaches the tip, then gently flick to remove air bubbles. Use the same method to fill puff pipettes with nicotine‑containing 1× aCSF (30 µM), omitting the syringe filter for the puff pipette.

steps.title: Set up perfusion and recording rig
steps.instruction: Power on the patch‑clamp rig (Axopatch 200B amplifier, Digidata 1550, Clampex 10.5). Begin perfusion of fresh oxygenated 1× aCSF into the recording chamber at 0.5–1 mL·min⁻¹ via gravity feed or peristaltic pump, direct waste line to a 2 L Erlenmeyer flask containing diluted bleach connected to a vacuum line. Gently place the slice in the recording chamber with a transfer pipette, secure it with a stainless‑steel harp, mount the patch and puff pipettes onto their headstages, and check slice viability.

steps.title: Perform whole‑cell patch‑clamp recording
steps.instruction: Apply positive pressure to the patch pipette, lower both pipettes into the bath, confirm pipette resistance (3–6 MΩ), bring pipettes above the selected neuron with micromanipulators, zero the pipette offset using the “membrane test” in Clampex, slowly descend the patch pipette until a small dimple and resistance increase are observed, release pressure and apply gentle suction at –40 mV to form a giga‑ohm seal, then hold at –70 mV and apply brief suction to achieve whole‑cell configuration. Set the amplifier to voltage‑clamp mode, begin gap‑free recording, position the puff pipette ~20 µm from the patched cell, deliver nicotine puffs (30 µM) using a picopritzer (PV800, WPI) at 5–10 psi (start low and adjust), typically 2–3 puffs are needed for a stable response, monitor capacitive transients and adjust compensation as needed.

steps.title: Clean equipment after recording
steps.instruction: Clean all tools, tubing, and perfusion lines with milli‑Q water and, where appropriate, 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Export and analyze data
steps.instruction: Export raw current traces from Clampfit or compatible acquisition software, analyze peak nicotine‑evoked current amplitudes in R or Python, compare peak amplitudes between MPEG4Ch‑treated and control IPN neurons (e.g., using t‑tests or linear mixed‑effects models as appropriate).

description: Precise manipulation of endogenous receptors in vivo remains a significant challenge in neuroscience, particularly in the context of physiology and behavior, due to the lack of specific pharmacological tools and the difficulty in achieving sustained and localized effects. The application of traditional pharmacological tools is particularly problematic in in vivo electrophysiology, as compounds must be pressure-injected during experiments, often prematurely ending the recording. The CATCH approach overcomes these limitations by enabling sustained, localized, and receptor-specific antagonism through a chemogenetic strategy, allowing for precise and long-lasting manipulation of neuronal signaling. This protocol is compatible with a variety of downstream applications, including ex vivo and in vivo electrophysiology and behavioral assays such as conditioned place preference, and can be adapted to other receptor systems with appropriate genetic targeting. For optimal reproducibility and interpretation, careful attention to experimental controls and validation steps is essential.
